messages:
Alex (support): Heads-up — ACME (private VPC) reports tenant charts empty in Console starting ~03:00 UTC. They say API calls succeed but no per-tenant metrics. Happened right after auth-proxy roll to 2.1.3. Ticket 98765. Can infra/ops triage?

ACME Support (customer): Confirmed — All usage shows in raw logs but Console shows zeros for organization 'acme-123'. We only see global totals.

Sam (eng-infra): Looking. Any chance headers are being dropped/rewritten en route to metrics collector? Which endpoint do they hit?

Alex (support): They POST to our private collector via gateway: POST https://private-gw.acme/v1/metrics/ingest. I asked them for a curl. Here's what they sent back (sanitized):

```
$ curl -i -X POST https://private-gw.acme/v1/metrics/ingest \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Org-ID: acme-123" \
  -d '{"events": [...]}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: auth-proxy/2.1.3
Date: Thu, 10 Mar 2026 03:12:01 GMT
X-Request-ID: rqd-abc123

# On the collector side logs we see ingestion but header payload shows:
Received headers: {"x-org-id": "-", "x-request-id": "rqd-abc123"}
```

Ravi (eng-runtime): That log line is suspicious — looks like the header got removed before reaching collector. I just checked the recent auth-proxy change: there was an Envoy filter tweak to remove internal headers for upstream vendors. Might be too broad.

Sam (eng-infra): Pulling proxy config now. 

Sam (eng-infra): Found route config for metrics cluster — it has a request header removal list: 

```
routes:
  - match:
      prefix: "/v1/metrics"
    route:
      cluster: metrics-collector
    request_headers_to_remove: ["x-org-id", "x-tenant", "x-internal-token"]
```

Sam (eng-infra): That explains it — rule was intended to prevent leaking internal auth to external vendors, but metrics-collector is an internal cluster and needs X-Org-ID to map telemetry.

Maya (prod-ops): Oof. Was this change part of auth-proxy 2.1.3? I see PR #432 added the remove list. It targeted third-party forwarders but matched the metrics route too.

Ravi (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigation: we can whitelist the metrics cluster by removing the header removal for that route, or add a preserve_header rule. I'll prepare a targeted fix and a canary.

Alex (support): Any repro steps we can give ACME to validate quickly?

Ravi (eng-runtime): Ask them to POST with X-Org-ID and we can tail collector logs with `grep` on request id. Example: 

```
curl -v -X POST https://private-gw.acme/v1/metrics/ingest \
  -H "X-Org-ID: acme-123" -H "X-Request-ID: test-123" -d '{"events":[]}'
# On gateway node run:
journalctl -u metrics-collector -f | grep test-123
```

Sam (eng-infra): I'll open a patch. Also enabling a fallback in collector: if X-Org-ID missing, try IP->tenant mapping for 48h. That buys time for backfill.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy auth-proxy 2.1.4 to private-gw-1 started (canary id: canary-20260310-1).

InfraBot: Observability alert suppressed for tenant gaps while we investigate (alert-id: OBS-tenant-gap-987).

ACME Support (customer): Ran the test with X-Request-ID=test-123. Collector log shows Test-123 arrived and header present now. Thank you.

Sam (eng-infra): Patch merged to main, rolling 2.1.4 to all private gateways with preserve rule for metrics cluster. Also enabled IP->tenant fallback in collector for 2 days.

Ravi (eng-runtime): We'll kick a backfill job to reconstruct per-tenant counters from raw events for the missing window (3:00–04:00). ETA ~45m.

ACME Support (customer): Confirmed dashboards are showing per-tenant counts again after ~30m. They look consistent with logs.

Alex (support): Great — will keep ticket open until backfill completes and then close. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
